question.worked_solution:
The residue of $-49$ modulo $7$ is the integer $0\le r<7$ such that

$$
-49≡r\,(\text{mod}\,7).
$$

**Method 1**

To find the residue $r,$ we need to write $-49$ as an integer multiple of $7,$ plus the residue $r.$

We note that $-49≡0\,(\text{mod}\,7)$ because

$$
-49=(-7)\cdot 7+0.
$$

Therefore, the residue of $-49$ modulo $7$ is $0.$

**Method 2**

We can use the addition property:

$$
\begin{aligned}-49 & ≡-49+0 &  & (\text{mod}\,7) \\  & ≡-49+7\cdot 7 &  & (\text{mod}\,7) \\  & ≡-49+49 &  & (\text{mod}\,7) \\  & ≡0 &  & (\text{mod}\,7)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the residue of $-49$ modulo $7$ is $0.$
